item.title: Takaichi Dominates Japan’s Lower House Election
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi’s landslide election win gives her a sweeping mandate to pursue a conservative policy agenda and sets the stage for a high-profile summit with President Trump.

item.title: U.S.-India and EU-India Trade Agreements: Who Won?
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch compares India's latest trade agreements with the United States and European Union.

item.title: Haiti Embarks on Another Rocky Political Transition
item.description: CSIS Americas Senior Associate Georges Fauriol and Mary Speck analyze Haiti’s future directions as the country’s Transitional Presidential Council ends and a new interim government takes office.

item.title: India’s New Ambitions on Trade Must Be Paired with Domestic Reform
item.description: India’s new trade confidence, marked by deals with the United States and the EU, signals a break from protectionism. But trade gains won’t stick without deep domestic reforms, especially at the state level, where land, labor, and power policies will decide success.

item.title: Takaichi Landslide Shows Limits of Chinese Economic Coercion
item.description: Philip Luck examines the recent Japanese election, highlighting how economic coercion against democracies can often strengthen government support and influence electoral outcomes.

item.title: What Is Next After the Suicide Attack in Pakistan?
item.description: This morning, a suicide bomber attacked a Shia mosque in Islamabad, Pakistan. The most likely perpetrator is the Islamic State–Khorasan Province, which operates both in Afghanistan and Pakistan but has a significant interest in mass-casualty international attacks.

item.title: CSIS Global Health Policy Center Names Ambassador Lisa Carty Non-Resident Senior Adviser
item.description: The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) today announced that Ambassador (retired) Lisa Carty has been appointed as a non-resident senior adviser with the CSIS Global Health Policy Center (GHPC).

item.title: Tracking China’s Increased Military Activities in the Indo-Pacific in 2025
item.description: Analysis of open-source data shows that China’s military activities in the Indo-Pacific region increased in both operational tempo and geographical reach.

item.title: States Weekly: February 4, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers February 4, 2026.
